mainEvent.title: Fri 11/20 · S&P 500 and Dow fall into a correction as the Nasdaq sinks 5.3%
mainEvent.body: The S&P 500 fell **3.70%** to 6,910.39 for a seventh straight loss, the longest streak since February 2020, and closed more than 10% below its Oct 6 record, a correction; the Dow lost 949.73 points (**1.93%**) to 48,147.33 and also closed in a correction, and the Nasdaq dropped **5.28%** to 22,617.73, erasing its 2026 gain (AP, Yahoo Finance, Reuters). For the week the S&P lost **8.6%**, the Dow 8.0% and the Nasdaq 10.0%, the worst week since April 2025. Nvidia plunged **14%** after Reuters reported the SEC is examining its accounting, the chip index fell 10.7%, and Anthropic lost 9% on its second day. Bonds rallied, with the 10Y down about 13bp to 4.92%, and the VIX touched 40 intraday. Next week: flash PMIs Monday, PCE inflation, and the Thanksgiving holiday Thursday.

regime.text: Fri 11/20: the AI selloff turned into a rout. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% for a seventh straight day and joined the Dow in a correction, the Nasdaq lost 5.3% and gave up its 2026 gain, and tech (XLK) fell 7.3% while only consumer staples rose. stories.title: S&P 500 and Dow fall into a correction; Nasdaq drops 5.3% and turns negative for 2026.
stories.body: The S&P 500 fell **3.70%** (265.44 points) to 6,910.39 Friday, its seventh straight loss and the longest losing streak since February 2020, leaving it more than 10% below its Oct 6 record of 7,818.93; the Dow lost **949.73 points** (1.93%) to 48,147.33, also in a correction, and the Nasdaq **5.28%** to 22,617.73, wiping out its gain for the year (AP via NPR, Yahoo Finance, Motley Fool). The Nasdaq 100 fell about 5.6% and the Russell 2000 about 2.5–2.8% (investingLive, Yahoo Finance). For the week the S&P lost **8.6%**, the Dow 8.0%, the Nasdaq 10.0% and the Russell 2000 7.5%, the worst week for the major indexes since April 2025 (Reuters via MarketScreener, investingLive). Tech (XLK) fell 7.3% and industrials 3.1%, while consumer staples (+0.7%) were the only sector up (sector ETFs); General Mills, HCA and UnitedHealth rose. Reasons cited: the reported SEC look at Nvidia's accounting, Anthropic's fade from its debut peak, worries about AI spending after midterm wins for candidates who want to slow data-center building, and a near-certain Fed hike in December (AP, Reuters, investingLive). The VIX touched 40 intraday (Bloomberg via ad-hoc-news), and CNN's Fear & Greed index fell to **9.7**, extreme fear, from 37 a week ago.

stories.title: Nvidia plunges 14% on a reported SEC accounting review; chips fall 10.7%.
stories.body: Nvidia fell **14.0%** to **$125.53** Friday, its ninth loss in 10 sessions and more than 25% below where it traded before Jensen Huang's exit earlier this month (Yahoo Finance, Motley Fool, AP), after Reuters reported that the SEC is examining its accounting practices; the SEC declined to comment and no wrongdoing has been found (Reuters via FinChannel, investingLive). The PHLX semiconductor index dropped **10.7%**: Micron fell 13.9%, AMD 13.3% and Broadcom about 12%, the latter also hit by an unconfirmed report that Google will cut next year's chip orders (AP, Motley Fool). CoreWeave lost 12.1%, Corning 10.9% and Bloom Energy 15.3%, and crypto miners such as IREN and Applied Digital fell 17–19% (investingLive, AP, 24/7 Wall St). Nvidia rose about 1% after hours (Yahoo Finance). Its fiscal Q3 beat on Nov 17 (revenue $115.8B, January-quarter guide $130B) did not stop the slide. The board has said it will not reinstate Huang, with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO; Polymarket gives about 5% that Huang rejoins by Dec 31 and about 20% that a permanent CEO is named by then (last trades this week).

stories.title: Anthropic falls 9% on day two but stays above its $83 IPO price.
stories.body: Anthropic (**ANT**) fell **9.1%** to **$88.30** Friday, its second day of trading, still above the $83 IPO price but about 23% below Thursday's $115.10 peak (AP, investingLive). On its debut Thursday it opened at **$111.50** at 11:48a and closed at $97.17, up 17% (StockTitan, FinanceFeeds). The listing has not lifted the AI trade: AP and Reuters cite its fade from the opening print as one trigger of the two-day selloff, and its big backers fell again Friday, with Amazon down 4.1% and Alphabet 2.6% (Motley Fool). Underwriters exercised their option on up to 147 million extra shares, lifting the total raised with the $26B private placement at $83 (Nvidia, Google, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom and others) to about **$119.5B**, the largest IPO ever (TNW, FinChannel). ARK Invest bought about $91M of shares after the debut (CNBC via TNW).

stories.title: Fed: Cook warns of falling behind as a December hike is all but priced in.
stories.body: Governor Lisa Cook said Friday in Santiago that "waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve" and that policy is not restrictive enough after September's hike (Yahoo Finance, investingLive). CME FedWatch puts about **97%** on a 25bp hike on Dec 9 (Yahoo Finance; BigGo, as of Nov 20), up from about 88.5% a week ago. Philadelphia Fed President Paulson said Thursday the Fed will need to hike again because inflation is too high (Reuters), and Governor Waller argued this week for a half-point move in December unless the Fed signals another hike in January (Yahoo Finance, Nov 18). Bonds rallied on the stock rout: the 10Y fell about **13bp** to 4.92% and the 2Y 13bp to 4.65% (Yahoo Finance, investingLive). The final November University of Michigan sentiment index came in at **51.5**, in line with forecasts and up from 48.0 in October, and one-year inflation expectations fell to **3.7%** from 4.3% in the preliminary survey and 4.7% in October (investingLive, Yahoo Finance). PCE inflation is due next week. Kalshi has a 25bp hike at 89% and a hold at 9%.

stories.title: CrowdStrike in talks to buy Zscaler; Zscaler jumps 17% after hours.
stories.body: CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire rival Zscaler, which has a market value of about **$33.5B**, according to two people familiar with the matter; no deal is guaranteed and terms were not reported (Reuters via Investing.com, 4:46p). Zscaler rose **17%** after hours and CrowdStrike fell **8%** (Reuters), after both lost more than 5% in the regular session (Reuters via MarketScreener, Investing.com). Elsewhere in earnings: Intuit, which fell more than 10% premarket Friday, guided Q2 revenue to $4.93–4.95B vs about $5.11B expected and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68B (company release, TradingKey); Ross raised its full-year EPS outlook but guided the next quarter softer (StockStory); and Gap rose about 2.5% premarket on Old Navy sales after cutting its outlook (Reuters). BJ's Wholesale earned $1.73 a share, helped by a roughly $240M card-fee settlement, with comparable club sales +13.5% (+4.1% ex-gas), and raised its full-year adjusted EPS guide to $5.10–5.30 (company release). Walmart rose 1.5% Friday after raising its outlook Thursday (Motley Fool).

stories.title: Oil rises Friday but posts a third weekly loss on a supply glut.
stories.body: The more active January WTI contract rose **1.2%** to settle at **$83.41** Friday, the expiring December contract 0.9% to $83.98, and Brent **0.6%** to **$92.57**, as traders weighed the risk of renewed US strikes on Iran (Bloomberg via Rigzone, AP). Brent still lost **3.4%** for the week, a third straight weekly drop, and is down about a fifth in November: the IEA sees a surplus of about 2 million barrels a day this quarter, Goldman flagged a glut next year, and Energy Secretary Chris Wright said flows through the Strait of Hormuz are at a record (Bloomberg via Rigzone). President Trump has said he is not rushing into a decision on Iran, and the FT reported he is weighing new strikes (via investingLive). Gold fell 3–4% to about $3,520 and copper 3% as the broader selloff hit commodities (Motley Fool, investingLive). OPEC+ meets Nov 29.
